report_title: Four- and eight-digit decimal helpers in lexical-parse-integer 1.0.6
selected_scope_from_report:
For every packed 32-bit or 64-bit word, the corresponding decimal-specialized
`is_4digits` or `is_8digits` body returns successfully and reports true exactly
when all four or eight bytes are ASCII decimal digits. For words satisfying
that condition, the corresponding `parse_4digits` or `parse_8digits` body
returns successfully with their positional decimal value, reading bytes from
least to most significant. For example, the bytes `1`, `2`, `3`, `4` decode
to 1234. These helper theorems do not establish complete or partial parsing.
limitations_from_report:
The checked bodies are decimal specializations of the published helpers: their
const `FORMAT` parameter is removed and the `NumberFormat::MANTISSA_RADIX`
lookup is replaced with `10u32`. A source checker confirms the rest of each
copied helper body matches the release. This supports correspondence for radix 10,
but Rust-to-Rust equivalence to the release has not been formally proved.

The decoder theorems assume all packed bytes are decimal digits. The
recognizer theorems characterize that condition, but their composition with
callers is not proved. Public parsing traits, overflow handling, and complete
or partial parser correctness are not established by these mappings. Aeneas rejects an outer-loop
break in the original complete parser, leaving that algorithm unproved.
